answer: In an agent economy each identity holds a stake at one vertex of a capability graph. Influence requires the agent to wander to a new vertex every few epochs. When local occupancy crosses a knoll threshold the protocol multiplies every occupant's required bond by the square of the excess density. An attacker adding heads must either accept diluted influence on crowded vertices or pay super-linearly rising stakes that cannot be bought in bulk or parallelized across a farm.
